prompt: Which feature of a velocity-time graph represents the displacement of a moving object?
options: The gradient of the graph line
The area between the graph line and the time axis
The vertical intercept on the velocity axis
The total length of the graph line

answer.explanation: The area between the velocity-time line and the time axis represents displacement because the product of velocity and time has units of metres (m s^-1 x s = m).

distractor_explanations: The gradient of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration, not displacement.
Correct: the signed area between the line and the time axis equals displacement.
The vertical intercept represents the initial velocity at time t = 0.
The line length has no kinematic significance and depends entirely on axis scales.
hints: Consider the physical units obtained when you multiply the quantities on the vertical and horizontal axes.
Units of m s^-1 multiplied by s yield metres, which is the unit of displacement.
solution: Option 2 is correct. Displacement equals the signed area bounded by the velocity-time graph line and the time axis.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Identify the vertical axis as velocity (m s^-1) and the horizontal axis as time (s).
Step 2: Note that an area on this graph represents the product of velocity and time: (m s^-1) x s = m.
Step 3: The metre is the SI unit of displacement, so the graph area represents displacement.
Step 4: Distinguish this from the gradient, which is (Delta v) / (Delta t) = m s^-2, representing acceleration.
